findings.title: Returned SQL fragments with a top-level OR are not parenthesized
findings.body: The org and team auth builders return `(A) OR (B)` with no outer parentheses (lines 171-174, 204-207). The eventTypeId filter does the same (`("eventTypeId" = X) OR ("eventParentId" = X)`, line 106). `getBaseConditions` only adds parentheses when both auth and filter fragments exist (line 73). With no filters it returns the bare OR at line 75. Any caller that appends to it, e.g. `WHERE ${base} AND "createdAt" >= ${start}`, gets `A OR (B AND date)` from SQL precedence, so the date range silently drops for team bookings. `getAuthorizationConditions` and `getFilterConditions` are public too. A caller that writes `${auth} AND ${filter}` gets `auth AND eventTypeId = X OR eventParentId = X`, which returns bookings outside the authorized scope. Nothing in the repo calls these methods yet, so nothing is broken today. Still, a method called `getBaseConditions` is clearly meant to be built on. Fix: have every builder wrap its result, e.g. `Prisma.sql`(${...})``, so each fragment can be combined safely.

findings.title: Two of the four branches in getBaseConditions can never run
findings.body: `getAuthorizationConditions()` always returns a `Prisma.Sql` object. Every path in `buildAuthorizationConditions` (lines 125-143) returns a Sql instance, even `NOTHING_CONDITION`, and an object is always truthy. So the `else if (filterConditions)` branch (76-77) and the final `else` (78-79) can never run. Worse, they suggest that filters alone could be applied without authorization. Simplify to `return filterConditions ? Prisma.sql`(${auth}) AND (${filter})` : auth;`.

findings.title: Constructor's public options type no longer catches a missing teamId for team scope
findings.body: `InsightsBookingServicePublicOptions` makes `teamId` optional for every scope. So `{ scope: "team", userId, orgId }` now compiles. At runtime the zod discriminated union (lines 21-26) rejects it, `this.options` becomes `null` (line 63), and every query quietly matches nothing (`1=0`). The old constructor took `InsightsBookingServiceOptions`, the discriminated union, so this mistake was a compile error. Keep the union as the parameter type, or make the public type a discriminated union, unless callers really need the loose shape.

findings.title: Caching tests removed while the caching code stays
findings.body: The PR deletes the `Caching` describe block. But `getAuthorizationConditions` and `getFilterConditions` still cache results in `cachedAuthConditions` and `cachedFilterConditions` (insightsBooking.ts:83-95), and nothing tests that behaviour now. The deleted tests only needed their expected values switched to `Prisma.sql`. They could also check that the second call returns the same object (`toBe`) instead of just an equal one, which would actually prove the cache is used.

findings.title: Only one raw-SQL query actually runs against the database (user scope)
findings.body: The new `ANY(${array})` fragments for org and team scope (insightsBooking.ts:164, 168, 201) are only checked as Sql object shapes (lines 295-299, 332-343). They are never run against Postgres. The single query that runs, `getBaseConditions`, uses user scope, so it never exercises the `ANY` array binding or the OR/AND grouping. Add a `$queryRaw` assertion for team or org scope with bookings that should and should not match. That would confirm the raw-SQL rewrite returns the same rows as the old Prisma `where` objects.

contracts.action: Replace `findMany` (Prisma where-object query on bookingTimeStatusDenormalized) with public `getBaseConditions()` returning a Prisma.Sql fragment for callers to embed in raw queries
contracts.equivalent_path: Old findMany merged `AND: [auth, filter]` into the caller's `where`, so Prisma kept the grouping. Sibling InsightsRoutingService still builds where-objects the same way.
contracts.before_after: Before, Prisma nested each condition inside AND/OR objects, so the grouping always held. After, callers splice text in, and the grouping only holds if every fragment is parenthesized. getBaseConditions wraps only the combined auth+filter case.
contracts.visible_effect: No production caller in the repo uses the service (a grep for InsightsBookingService matches only the service and its test). So nothing visible changes yet; the only consumer is the integration test's `$queryRaw` at line 481.
contracts.failure_mode: If a future caller appends conditions after a bare OR fragment, filters get dropped silently because of SQL precedence (reported as a finding). An invalid option or a non-admin user returns `1=0`, so the result is empty and no error is raised.

summary:
This PR changes `InsightsBookingService` to build `Prisma.sql` fragments instead of Prisma where-objects, and replaces `findMany` with `getBaseConditions`. For each scope the logic matches the old where-objects. The column names exist on `BookingTimeStatusDenormalized`, and the rewritten `isOrgOwnerOrAdmin` check behaves the same. Nothing in the repo calls the service yet, so nothing users see changes today.

The main risk is how the fragments combine. The org and team auth fragments, and the eventTypeId filter, end in a top-level OR without outer parentheses, and `getBaseConditions` returns them as-is when there are no filters. Any future caller that appends conditions will hit SQL operator precedence. `getBaseConditions` also has two branches that can never run.

The new public options type no longer catches a missing `teamId` at compile time for team scope. In the tests, the caching tests were removed and only user scope is run against the database. I rated all five findings as "consider"; none blocks the merge.
